title: A Multi-Objective Approach to Curriculum-Based Course Timetabling with Continuity Across Semesters
summary: We study a curriculum-based university course timetabling problem in which the preferences of two key stakeholder groups - lecturers and students - must be balanced while maintaining continuity across semesters in a weekly repeating timetable. While existing approaches typically rely on single-objective formulations or aggregate multiple objectives into a weighted sum, this can obscure the underlying trade-offs between conflicting stakeholder preferences.
